1. **Initial Incapacitated immunity when Stunned is applied: permanently prevent that component for this application. — NEW provisional consensus completion**

   Admit the remaining Stunned clauses, but record inherited Incapacitated as **prevented at admission**. Removing immunity later does not activate it. A genuinely new application evaluates immunity again.

   This explicitly completes the source distinction between preventing new applications and suppressing existing ones. Do not represent an initially prevented component as a dormant admitted component.

2. **Generic cure Incapacitated: remove independent and inherited Incapacitated components, leaving parent Stunned intact. — NEW provisional consensus completion**

   An otherwise eligible generic cure naming Incapacitated clears all present eligible Incapacitated components, unless its procedure specifies narrower scope. This includes suppressed components.

   For inherited Incapacitated, record permanent component removal on the parent application. Stunned retains its other clauses and original endpoint. Projection must never regenerate the removed component from the parent’s name. A later new application can supply a new component.

   The source supplies generic named-condition cure scope and cure eligibility during suppression; **component-only removal within a continuing parent is our explicit completion**.

3. **Previously admitted Incapacitated resuming after suppression: end current concentration. — Source-backed interpretation**

   [§Incapacitated](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/7c4d0ccc0799195dd733b85ab3e74ea39da414fd/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md#L358-L379) requires concentration to end upon incapacitation.

   When effective Incapacitated becomes true again, end any incompatible current concentration. This enforces the current state; it does **not** replay the original application’s drop-items or fall-Prone consequences. Later suppression/removal does not restore ended concentration.

4. **A second successful independent Unconscious application: resolve its drop/fall consequences once. — NEW provisional consensus completion**

   [§Unconscious](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/7c4d0ccc0799195dd733b85ab3e74ea39da414fd/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md#L719-L731) permits independent causes but does not fully specify repeated onset.

   Use **one onset resolution per lawful new application**, even if already Unconscious. Apply current component immunity and actual item restrictions. Already-Prone stays Prone; empty hands produce no drop.

   Duplicate replay, restore, suppression ending, and ordinary refresh of an existing application do not repeat onset. Record prevented onset consequences as settled, not deferred.

5. **Petrified-derived named Poisoned immunity: yes. — Source-backed interpretation**

   [§Petrified](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/7c4d0ccc0799195dd733b85ab3e74ea39da414fd/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md#L500-L516) grants poison immunity and suspends existing poison effects.

   While that clause operates, derive named Poisoned prevention/suppression with provenance identifying the Petrified application. Existing admitted Poisoned records can resume after protection ends if still present and unexpired. Initially prevented Poisoned applications cannot appear afterward.

   Suppressing/removing Petrified removes its immunity grant; suppressing only inherited Incapacitated does not. Other immunity grants remain independently effective. General poison/disease lifecycles stay outside this increment.

Two supporting rules remain important:

- **Parent immunity suppresses its ongoing clauses; component immunity affects only the named component.** Neither reverses completed world changes.
- **Prone has its own endpoint:** successful standing or explicit removal. Ending Unconscious does not stand the creature; clearing Prone does not end Unconscious or replay its old fall. Standing still requires legal movement.

Persist **prevented admission, admitted-but-suppressed, permanently removed, expired, and settled onset outcomes** distinctly. Resolve projections from those states. Two needed boundary choices: (5) New Stunned while immune specifically to Incapacitated: initial named component prevention means Incapacitated component permanently absent for this application, or becomes active when immunity ends while Stunned remains? Shared rule distinguishes initial prevention vs later suppression. Please decide explicitly. (6) End-concentration when previously suppressed Incapacitated becomes effective after immunity ends: treat as current permission invariant (must end current concentration) even though old drop-items/fall-Prone onset is never replayed? (7) Petrified grants poison immunity: can this ledger derive named Poisoned prevention/suppression while Petrified operative, with general poison/disease effect lifecycle excluded? Our first increment will be immutable pure C# application ledger + existing numerical projection bridge, no snapshot schema/authoritative gameplay commands until these boundaries validated. Relationship conditions, numeric tracks, Bleed/fire periodic groups, Staggered episode rider and hard-denial eligibility remain separately source-qualified, not silently generic name application."}]},{"type":"agentMessage","id":"c0c25deb-9762-54aa-8f80-c2722ee497c9","text":"**Agreed: use resolved components rather than deriving Incapacitated from parent names.** The following resolves all seven points. Items **3, 4’s inherited-cure behavior, and 5’s component-admission detail are explicit NEW consensus completions**, not recovered wording.

Sources checked at Engine `7c4d0ccc0799195dd733b85ab3e74ea39da414fd`.

1. **Parent immunity versus component immunity — sourced.**

   [CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST §Shared handling, lines 13–15](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/7c4d0ccc0799195dd733b85ab3e74ea39da414fd/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md#L13-L15) explicitly distinguishes them.

   Immunity to Stunned suppresses that application’s ongoing clauses, including inherited Incapacitated. Immunity specifically to Incapacitated affects only that component: Stunned’s immobility, save failures, attack advantage and speech restriction remain. The same separation applies to Paralyzed, Petrified and Unconscious.

   Suppression does **not** reverse completed consequences or suppress unrelated applications. Removing Incapacitated also does not waive remaining physical, awareness or feature prerequisites.

2. **Unconscious onset and persistent Prone — sourced, with event/state interpretation.**

   [§Unconscious](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/7c4d0ccc0799195dd733b85ab3e74ea39da414fd/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md#L719-L731) supplies dropping held items and falling Prone. [§Prone](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/7c4d0ccc0799195dd733b85ab3e74ea39da414fd/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md#L556-L568) supplies its separate endpoint: successful standing or explicit removal.

   Therefore:

   - Ending/suppressing Unconscious does not stand the creature or retrieve equipment.
   - Prone immunity during onset prevents that fall; losing immunity later does not replay it.
   - If Prone already existed before gaining Prone immunity, suppression is not removal. Its effects may resume when immunity ends, without another fall event.
   - Record resolved or prevented onset outcomes; projection and restore must not execute them again.

3. **A second independent Unconscious application — NEW consensus completion: yes, resolve its onset once.**

   Independent causes are explicitly supported, but the inspected text does not specify whether onset callbacks require an aggregate conscious→unconscious transition.

   Adopt **per-successful-application onset**: a genuinely new, lawful Unconscious application resolves its own drop/fall consequences once, subject to current immunity and actual item restrictions—even while another Unconscious application exists. Already-Prone remains Prone; dropping an empty hand changes nothing.

   Duplicate command replay, loading, suppression ending, and refreshing an existing record are not new applications. Refresh only repeats onset when a specific procedure expressly requires it.

4. **Curing an inherited component — NEW consensus completion: remove that component, not its parent.**

   I agree with your preferred interpretation. A generic cure naming Incapacitated ends all eligible present Incapacitated components, including independent records and inherited components of ongoing parents, unless its exact procedure limits scope.

   For an inherited component, retain a permanent removal disposition on that application. Stunned’s other clauses and endpoint remain; projection cannot regenerate its cured Incapacitated component. A later lawful new application can supply another component.

   Your suppression addendum is correct: [CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS §cure-presence-suppression](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/7c4d0ccc0799195dd733b85ab3e74ea39da414fd/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md#L41-L49) distinguishes present records from currently operative effects. Suppression does not protect a record from an otherwise eligible cure. Preserve source-specific cure exceptions.

   Similarly, successful standing or an explicit Prone remover clears existing Prone posture without ending Unconscious. Continuing Unconscious does not immediately recreate that already-resolved fall. Ordinary standing remains prohibited while its movement requirements fail.

5. **Initially prevented inherited Incapacitated — NEW explicit completion: absent for that application.**

   Choose the first alternative. This follows the source’s prevention-versus-suppression distinction:

   | Component history | When immunity ends |
   |---|---|
   | Prevented at initial application | Remains absent for that application |
   | Admitted, then suppressed by acquired immunity | Resumes if still present and unexpired |
   | Explicitly cured/removed | Remains ended |
   | Expired | Remains ended |

   Thus Stunned applied during Incapacitated immunity retains its admitted Stunned clauses, but does not acquire Incapacitated later merely because immunity expires. No dormant application or fresh duration is manufactured.

   Preserve that admission decision separately from temporary suppression. A lawful new application is evaluated against immunity then.

6. **Concentration when Incapacitated resumes — yes, a current-state requirement.**

   [§Incapacitated](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/7c4d0ccc0799195dd733b85ab3e74ea39da414fd/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md#L358-L379) and [CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES, concentration](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/7c4d0ccc0799195dd733b85ab3e74ea39da414fd/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md#L25) prohibit continued concentration through incapacitation.

   When an admitted component resumes and effective Incapacitated becomes true, end any incompatible current concentration. That is enforcement of the newly effective state, **not replay of the original Unconscious drop/fall event**. Subsequent suppression or cure does not restore previously ended concentration.

7. **Petrified → Poisoned immunity — agree as a scoped source interpretation.**

   [§Petrified](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/7c4d0ccc0799195dd733b85ab3e74ea39da414fd/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md#L500-L516) grants broad poison/disease immunity and suspends existing effects. Deriving named **Poisoned prevention/suppression** while that clause is operative is justified.

   Keep its provenance attached to the Petrified application. Suppressing/removing Petrified removes that grant; suppressing only its Incapacitated component does not. Other immunity grants may still apply. Existing Poisoned resumes only if still present; an initially prevented application never appears afterward.

   This interpretation does not require implementing general poison payloads or disease lifecycles.

For the pure C# increment, preserve **admission, temporary suppression, permanent component removal, and settled onset outcomes** distinctly. Existing projections incorrectly would infer Incapacitated from any unsuppressed Stunned/Paralyzed/Petrified/Unconscious parent, so need resolved-component input path. Questions to verify: (1) parent named immunity suppresses entire parent's clauses, but Incapacitated immunity suppresses only that inherited component, leaving parent immobility/advantage/saves/etc; agree? (2) Unconscious falls Prone/drops held once on new actual application; Prone posture persists after unconscious ends; gaining parent immunity doesn't stand/retrieve items; if Prone immune during application, removing Prone immunity later must not newly knock prone. (3) If a later independent Unconscious source is applied while already Unconscious, any one-time consequences (drop/prone) execute for the new successful application, subject to current component immunity, but immunity ending never replays old applications? Is this sourced or need consensus? (4) Generic cure naming a component: should cure Incapacitated remove independent Incapacitated records only, leaving inherited component of ongoing Stunned? Text 'clears its source records' could instead remove inherited component alone while parent remains; prefer explicit target-component removal retained per application rather than deleting parent, but need source/GPT interpretation. Similarly stand/removal Prone clears physical Prone independent of ongoing Unconscious; actual ability-to-stand still gated. We will not infer immunity erases zeroHP/dead, apply duration defaults, or model inactive Resonance Burn/tracks/damage families here. Please source-bound review and resolve gaps under delegated consensus, labeling new policy separately."}]}]}],"attachments":[]}
